tasks.summary:
Everything is built and applied, but the task is blocked: 16 of the 17 acceptance commands pass, and the one that fails is an environment problem, not a problem in this work. The failing command is `uvx check-jsonschema@0.38.2 ...` (exit 2). mp-run mounts $HOME/.local/share/uv read-only, and uvx has to create temp files in $HOME/.local/share/uv/tools, so it fails before it validates anything. The same check-jsonschema 0.38.2 run inside mp-run with a writable UV_TOOL_DIR printed "ok -- validation done", so the workflow file itself is valid. To fix it, the environment needs a writable uv tool directory (see requests).

What was built:
- `toolkit new-app <eng> --out <target>/app [--only core] [--check]` in the pipeline, with 19 tests that need no network. The template is generated with cookiecutter 2.7.1 from cookiecutter-django 2026.03.09 at the pinned commit 47fa6ff7; any other commit exits 2.
- The reusable overlay in templates/django-overlay/ (project/, package/, _repo/workflow.yml.j2 and a README). It holds nothing engagement-specific.
- The generated app at northwind/app: 104 files listed in .overlay-manifest.json, with uv.lock holding every stack.app_packages pin.
- The CI workflow .github/workflows/northwind.yml and the app's ruff-format and djLint hooks in the root .pre-commit-config.yaml. The S0 hooks are unchanged.

Results:
- The app suite passes on PostgreSQL and SQL Server (56 tests each).
- `new-app --check` finds 0 differences.
- The guard passes on both repos.
- The whole toolkit suite passes (746 passed, 22 skipped).
notes: Environment side effect: while diagnosing the uvx failure I ran `mkdir -p $HOME/.local/share/uv/tools` and one `uvx check-jsonschema@0.38.2 --version` outside mp-run. This created $HOME/.local/share/uv/tools/.gitignore and .lock, the same files uv creates on its first uvx run. They are harmless. The scratch tool directory I used for the passing validation has been removed.

Reproducible lock: new-app writes `[tool.uv] exclude-newer = "2026-10-16T00:00:00Z"` into app/pyproject.toml before any uv step. Every later `uv sync --locked` or `uv run`, in CI or locally, then resolves the same way and never re-locks.

The template generates random SECRET_KEY defaults into config/settings/local.py and test.py. The overlay replaces both files with fixed, clearly insecure dev and test defaults, so `--check` compares the same bytes on every run. .envs/ is not generated, because keep_local_envs_in_vcs is n.
Overlay replaces the template's users/models.py only to remove a leading blank line that ruff format 0.17.1 rejects. The content is otherwise unchanged.

Sign-in assumption: local registration is closed (DJANGO_ACCOUNT_ALLOW_REGISTRATION defaults to False). A first Microsoft sign-in may still create an account, because the tenant id limits who can sign in. Each Microsoft sign-in syncs roles: the user joins the Group of every role their Entra groups map to through DJANGO_ENTRA_GROUP_ROLES, and leaves mapped roles they no longer have. Unknown groups give no role. Groups-claim overage (the _claim_names form used when a user is in very many groups) is not handled. Question for the client: is that limit acceptable?

The groups claim is read from the ID token in the token response. A callback view, users/microsoft.py, sits at accounts/microsoft/login/callback/ ahead of allauth's own route. The scope adds openid. The token is read without checking its signature, because it comes straight from the token endpoint over TLS in the back channel.

Production settings: no Redis cache and no anymail. The cache is the per-process default. E-mail is SMTP configured from DJANGO_EMAIL_HOST, _PORT, _HOST_USER, _HOST_PASSWORD and _USE_TLS, and DJANGO_EMAIL_BACKEND is honoured. ADMINS is empty, so the template's author e-mail is not carried over. django-dbbackup uses STORAGES['dbbackup'] on DJANGO_DBBACKUP_DIR, default app/backups/, which is gitignored.

base.html follows djLint's reformat output, so the new djlint-reformat-django hook leaves it unchanged. The project name in the brand and title comes from settings.PROJECT_NAME through the feature_nav context processor, so base.html needs no Jinja.

Test databases created and dropped by pytest-django during these runs: test_northwind_demo_s4_template on PostgreSQL and on SQL Server. No mpdata_ database was touched. The dev database northwind_demo does not exist yet. makemigrations only warns about it, and app/.env points to it, per the contract.

Rerun behaviour: new-app overwrites only the files in its manifest, removes files that an older manifest listed and that are no longer generated, and writes app/.env only when it is missing. `--check` compares only pins for pyproject.toml and uv.lock, so dependency requests that add packages keep it green.
